1.question:
What is the name and description of the business topic you want to create?

Please provide:
1. **Topic name** — a short, clear label (e.g. "Customer Churn & Retention", "Opal AI Adoption", "Sales Pipeline Health")
2. **Description** — 2–4 sentences explaining what this topic covers, what business question it answers, and who the primary audience is (e.g. Sales, CS, Product, Marketing, Finance)
1.answer: Experiment Statistical Methodology. Covers: Experiment Statistical Methodology, A/B Experimentation, Opti ID & Product Instance Management

selected.description: Tracks statistical configuration choices made per experiment: model type (frequentist / Bayesian), CUPED variance reduction, guardrail metrics, and outlier filtering. Primary dataset: STATS_MODELS_EXP.

4.question:
Which metrics and KPIs should the **Experiment Statistical Methodology** topic track?

These are the measures the AI will surface when users ask about statistical model adoption, CUPED usage, guardrail configuration, and experiment quality. Pre-selected items are either directly connected to your chosen concepts via graph `measured-by` edges, or serve as essential adoption-rate denominators.

⚠️ **Important:** The four core KPIs for this topic — `% Experiments Using Bayesian Model`, `CUPED Adoption Rate`, `Guardrail Metric Adoption Rate`, and `Outlier Filtering Adoption Rate` — **do not yet exist** as pre-built metrics in the app. They are pre-marked as custom KPIs to create, derived from the `STATS_MODELS_EXP` dataset selected in Step 3.

selected.label: ⭐ Exp Purple Button Clicked
selected.description: Tracks the number of times the experiment creation button is clicked in the Optimizely UI — a leading signal for new experiment volume entering the statistical model pipeline.
selected.ai_reasoning: The only metric in the graph with a confirmed `measured-by` edge to a selected concept (A/B Experimentation); serves as the top-of-funnel volume signal for experiments that will later carry statistical methodology configurations.

selected.label: ⭐ EXP - Engaged Accounts - Monthly
selected.description: Monthly count of customer accounts actively running experiments across all experiment types.
selected.ai_reasoning: Essential denominator for computing statistical methodology adoption rates (e.g. '% of engaged accounts using Bayesian model') — without this baseline population metric, feature-specific adoption percentages cannot be calculated.

selected.label: ⭐ EXP - Engaged Accounts - WX - Monthly
selected.description: Monthly count of engaged Web Experimentation (WX) accounts.
selected.ai_reasoning: WX-specific denominator needed to compute statistical methodology adoption rates within the Web Experimentation product line, which is the primary surface for `STATS_MODELS_EXP` data selected in Step 3.

selected.label: ⭐ EXP - Engaged Accounts - FX - Monthly
selected.description: Monthly count of engaged Feature Experimentation (FX) accounts.
selected.ai_reasoning: FX-specific denominator enabling cross-product-line comparison of `OUTLIER_FILTERING_ENABLED` adoption between WX and FX — a direct analytical axis in STATS_MODELS_EXP and FX Flag Raw data.

selected.label: ⭐ Cumulative Accounts - Ratio Metric - WX
selected.description: Cumulative count of WX accounts that have created at least one ratio metric.
selected.ai_reasoning: Ratio metrics are an advanced statistical configuration closely coupled to Bayesian and CUPED features; this is the best existing proxy in the metric library for measuring sophisticated statistical methodology adoption in WX.

selected.label: ⭐ Cumulative Accounts - Ratio Metric - FX
selected.description: Cumulative count of FX accounts that have created at least one ratio metric.
selected.ai_reasoning: FX counterpart to the WX ratio metric measure — enables side-by-side comparison of advanced statistical feature adoption between both experimentation product lines selected in Step 3.

selected.label: ⭐ Cumulative Accounts - Metric Created Using Filtering on Event Properties - WX
selected.description: Cumulative count of WX accounts that have created metrics with event-property filtering enabled.
selected.ai_reasoning: Event-property filtering is the closest existing proxy signal for `OUTLIER_FILTERING_ENABLED` adoption in WX; useful as a leading indicator of statistical sophistication while the dedicated outlier filtering KPI is being built.

selected.label: ⭐ Cumulative Accounts - Metric Created Using Filtering on Event Properties - FX
selected.description: Cumulative count of FX accounts that have created metrics with event-property filtering enabled.
selected.ai_reasoning: FX counterpart for event-property filtering adoption — paired with the WX version above, this enables complete cross-product-line outlier filtering analysis from the datasets selected in Step 3.

selected.label: ➕ % Experiments Using Bayesian Model [New KPI]
selected.description: Percentage of experiments where `STATS_MODEL_TYPE = 'bayesian'` out of all experiments with a recorded statistical model in `STATS_MODELS_EXP`. Can be segmented by `CREATED_MONTH` to track adoption trend over time.
selected.ai_reasoning: This is the primary adoption KPI for this topic and does not exist in the metric library — it is the direct numerator/rate expression of the `STATS_MODEL_TYPE` column that the Experiment Statistical Methodology concept is built around.

selected.label: ➕ CUPED Adoption Rate [New KPI]
selected.description: Percentage of experiments with `IS_CUPED = TRUE` in `STATS_MODELS_EXP`. Measures uptake of CUPED variance reduction. Can be trended monthly using `CREATED_MONTH`.
selected.ai_reasoning: CUPED adoption rate is a core KPI for this topic (`IS_CUPED` column in `STATS_MODELS_EXP`) and has no pre-built metric in the app — defining it here creates the measurement anchor the AI will use when answering any CUPED-related questions.

selected.label: ➕ Guardrail Metric Adoption Rate [New KPI]
selected.description: Percentage of experiments with `HAS_GUARDRAIL = TRUE` in `STATS_MODELS_EXP`. Measures how many experiments have at least one guardrail metric configured to protect against regressions.
selected.ai_reasoning: Guardrail metric adoption is a key product health signal stored directly in the `HAS_GUARDRAIL` column of `STATS_MODELS_EXP` — this KPI does not exist yet and is critical for the AI to answer any guardrail configuration questions.

selected.label: ➕ Outlier Filtering Adoption Rate [New KPI]
selected.description: Percentage of experiments (WX) or feature flags (FX) with `OUTLIER_FILTERING_ENABLED = TRUE` across `STATS_MODELS_EXP` and `FX Flag Raw data`. Enables cross-product-line comparison.
selected.ai_reasoning: Outlier filtering adoption spans both WX and FX product lines (two datasets selected in Step 3) and has no pre-built metric — creating this KPI unlocks the cross-product-line comparison analysis that is a stated goal of this topic.

7.question:
Are there terms in the **Experiment Statistical Methodology** topic that could be confused with other meanings?

The AI detected **6 ambiguous terms** across the concepts, datasets, and KPIs selected in Steps 2–5. Each rule below tells the AI how to interpret that term **within this topic only**. Review, confirm, or deselect any that don't match your intended meaning — and add your own if you spot a gap.

selected.label: "Model" = statistical inference type (frequentist or Bayesian) — NOT an Opal AI/ML model
selected.description: In this topic, "model" always refers to the STATS_MODEL_TYPE column in STATS_MODELS_EXP — either 'frequentist' or 'bayesian'. It must never be interpreted as an Opal large language model, an ML prediction model, or a data schema. If a user asks "which model is most popular among customers?", the AI must answer using STATS_MODEL_TYPE distribution — not Opal agent or thread usage data.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both Experiment Statistical Methodology and Opal AI concepts are in scope across this topic's selected datasets; in an AI-first product context, "model" is critically overloaded and will generate incorrect answers without an explicit disambiguation rule.

selected.label: "Experiment" (unqualified) = Web Experimentation (WX) A/B test via STATS_MODELS_EXP — NOT an FX feature flag test
selected.description: STATS_MODELS_EXP is a WX-only dataset. When a user asks about "experiments" without specifying product line, the AI should default to WX experiments (STATS_MODELS_EXP + OA_EXPERIMENTATION_UNIFIED). FX feature flag tests should be explicitly qualified as "FX experiments" or "feature flags" to prevent denominator mixing. If cross-product comparison is intended, the user should say "WX and FX experiments".
selected.ai_reasoning: STATS_MODELS_EXP contains only WX experiments; conflating WX and FX experiment counts when computing Bayesian or CUPED adoption rates would produce inflated or deflated percentages that cannot be reconciled back to either product line.

selected.label: "Adoption rate" for the 4 custom KPIs = experiment-level percentage (% of experiments), NOT account-level (% of accounts)
selected.description: The four custom KPIs created in Step 4 (% Experiments Using Bayesian Model, CUPED Adoption Rate, Guardrail Metric Adoption Rate, Outlier Filtering Adoption Rate) are all **experiment-level** rates: numerator = experiments with the flag TRUE, denominator = all experiments in STATS_MODELS_EXP. The EXP Engaged Accounts metrics also selected in Step 4 are **account-level** measures. These are different denominators and should never be combined without explicit segmentation. If a user asks "what is CUPED adoption?", return the experiment-level rate by default.
selected.ai_reasoning: Step 4 selected both experiment-level custom KPIs (from STATS_MODELS_EXP) and account-level engagement metrics (EXP Engaged Accounts - Monthly/WX/FX) in the same topic; without this rule, the AI risks mixing denominators when computing or comparing adoption figures.

selected.label: "Outlier Filtering" adoption = cross-product metric spanning STATS_MODELS_EXP (WX) AND FX Flag Raw data (FX) — report both side by side
selected.description: The custom Outlier Filtering Adoption Rate KPI (Step 4) intentionally spans both product lines, as OUTLIER_FILTERING_ENABLED exists in both STATS_MODELS_EXP (WX) and FX Flag Raw data (FX). When a user asks about outlier filtering adoption without specifying a product line, the AI must report WX and FX figures separately and compare them — not silently return only the WX number from STATS_MODELS_EXP.
selected.ai_reasoning: This shared column name across two selected datasets is the most structurally risky ambiguity in this topic; defaulting to one product line without disclosure would undercount or misrepresent total outlier filtering usage across the customer base.

selected.label: "Guardrail" = HAS_GUARDRAIL experiment configuration flag (statistical) — NOT an Opal AI content-safety guardrail
selected.description: In this topic, "guardrail" exclusively refers to a secondary metric attached to an experiment that must not regress for the experiment to be considered a success (HAS_GUARDRAIL = TRUE in STATS_MODELS_EXP). It is completely unrelated to Opal AI's content safety guardrails or product-level feature policies. If a user asks "how many experiments use guardrails?", the AI must query HAS_GUARDRAIL in STATS_MODELS_EXP — not Opal safety or compliance logs.
selected.ai_reasoning: Product - EXP - Opal Managed Experiments and AI Assisted Experiments datasets are in scope (selected in Steps 3–5), making the AI safety interpretation of "guardrail" a realistic mis-routing risk without an explicit rule.

selected.label: "Opal-managed experiment" (IS_EXPERIMENT_OPAL_MANAGED = TRUE) ≠ "AI-assisted experiment" (AI Assisted Experiments dataset) — overlapping but distinct categories
selected.description: An **Opal-managed experiment** (IS_EXPERIMENT_OPAL_MANAGED = TRUE in OA_EXPERIMENTATION_UNIFIED; sourced from Product - EXP - Opal Managed Experiments) is fully automated end-to-end by Opal AI — Opal owns the entire experiment lifecycle. An **AI-assisted experiment** (AI Assisted Experiments - Experiment dataset) is one where Opal AI contributed a variant, description, or configuration element, but a human retains ownership. An experiment can be both, either, or neither. Do not treat these as synonyms when segmenting statistical methodology adoption by AI involvement.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both datasets were selected in Step 3 and serve as segmentation dimensions for methodology adoption; treating them as interchangeable would misrepresent the degree of human oversight — a key variable for understanding whether Opal or humans are driving statistical configuration choices.

8.question:
How should the **Experiment Statistical Methodology** topic grow over time as the graph evolves?

This policy controls how the AI automatically expands your topic when new datasets, metrics, concepts, or events are added to Optimizely Analytics. Choose the expansion depth and trust threshold that match your team's governance tolerance.

selected.label: ⚖️ Moderate — Depth 2, human-confirmed (Recommended)
selected.description:
The topic automatically **proposes** — but does not activate — entities that are 2 graph hops from your 5 root concepts, provided they carry a `human-confirmed` or higher trust score. An admin reviews and approves each proposal before it becomes part of the topic's AI context.

**What this unlocks at depth 2 for this topic:**
- Concepts reachable via A/B Experimentation: **Opal AI Content Generation** (AI-managed experiment configurations), **Feature Adoption Tracking** (statistical feature uptake signals)
- Datasets reachable via Feature Experimentation (FX): **FX Status Timeseries** (longitudinal outlier filtering trends)
- Metrics reachable via EXP Engaged Accounts: **EXP Engaged ARR — WX/FX** (ARR weighting of adoption rates)

**Best for:** Most teams. Allows the topic to grow with the product without requiring manual curation of every new entity, while keeping a human review gate before the AI uses any expansion.
selected.ai_reasoning: Moderate is the right default for this topic because the statistical methodology space is actively evolving (new model types, CUPED enhancements, FX parity work), so the topic will need to grow — but the 6 disambiguation rules confirmed in Step 7 show the topic has meaningful ambiguity risk that warrants human review before new entities are activated.
